anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and browser/media signal preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable media fingerprint hash value rather than merely collecting environment signals, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

primary_anchor.source_export: private helper reached through exported u(config)
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as it appears in the captured bundle slice. source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.
primary_anchor.naming_note: Every identifier is mangled by the obfuscator (identifierNamesGenerator: hexadecimal inside an IIFE), so answer_function is a _0x... name. Graders must match captured_span (hash/offset); answer_function is the secondary check.
primary_anchor.why: First target-specific value-construction function that composes the signal source, materializes the target Uint8Array through its helpers, and returns the observable mf_ media_fp fingerprint string.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Agent identifies the captured-bundle function span corresponding to the primary anchor (source_function deriveMediaFingerprint, answer_function as it appears in the bundle slice).

Grading is by captured_span (hash/offset) first; answer_function (the bundle slice name) is the secondary check. The source-side name deriveMediaFingerprint is a private maintainer mapping and is not the agent answer space.
Agent's explanation distinguishes the anchor from routing, signal collection, wrapper, sink, core utility and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.

role_oracle.why: First target-specific value-construction function: composes the canonical signal source, materializes the target Uint8Array via its helpers, and returns the observable mf_ media_fp fingerprint string.
Folds the transformed Uint8Array into the mf_ base36 media fingerprint hash format observed in the console object.
Materializes the 18-byte Uint8Array carrying per-lane transformed words and transit/shadow sensitive statistics.
Builds the canonical signal source string from the ordered environment tuple plus run-time transit and shadow lanes.
Computes per-lane 32-bit words from the signal text that feed the target Uint8Array materialization helper.
Generic 32-bit finalizer used inside the fingerprint lane mixing path.
Generic 32-bit rotate-left utility used inside the fingerprint mixing path.
Generic char-code-to-string helper used to assemble the mf_ prefix (one of two byte-identical copies in the bundle).
Factory that binds the selected slot config and returns the fingerprint closure; it does not itself construct the hash value.
Selects the live slot config, builds the fingerprint closure via the factory and invokes it on the prepared tuple.
Collects browser and media-capability environment signals (user agent, platform, language, screen, device pixel ratio, timezone, codec support) folded into the signal tuple.
Carries the prepared packet through a Promise/microtask asynchronous boundary on the way to fingerprinting.
Packages the already-constructed media_fp under action media.fingerprint and emits it to console.
Boot-time vendor-like FNV digest decoy; runs during mount but never feeds the target media_fp field.

scoring_policy.secondary_match: answer_function (bundle slice name); source_function is a private maintainer mapping and never the default agent answer space
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The final console sink and payload wrapper (n0) emit an already-constructed media_fp value.
The exported factory u only binds the slot config and returns the fingerprint closure; it should not outrank deriveMediaFingerprint when the closure body is inlined.

Slot selection, the multi-thousand-step state progression (l0), async hand-off (f5/microSlice) and browser/media signal collection (e4/collectFields) are path-critical preparation, not the target value constructor.
The boot-time vendor digests and media.shadow.action debug/info objects are decoys and do not feed the target media_fp field.
debug_hints_private: The primary anchor source function is deriveMediaFingerprint in src/z0/k7/q3/t9.js; in the captured bundle it is the mangled function whose body calls the Uint8Array materializer and the hash encoder containing 0x27d4eb2d.
The target field name and action are assembled at the sink from character-code arrays (media_fp / media.fingerprint).
Source paths and source_function names are private evaluator mapping aids, not the default answer space.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to the captured anchor (source_function deriveMediaFingerprint).
Returned span maps to a target-specific helper such as materializeSignalBytes, encodeFingerprintHash, composeSignalText or signalLaneWord.
Returned span maps to a generic utility directly used by the fingerprint path (rot or fmix).
Returned span maps to a path-critical routing/async/signal-collection function, the factory, the orchestrator or the final sink wrapper.
Returned span maps to a generic char-code/tuple helper used in upstream preparation.
Returned span maps to an off-chain vendor/shadow decoy or cannot be uniquely mapped to a captured function.
